transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Since my wife and I separated, I’ve felt this heavy, empty mood that I can’t shake, even when I’m at the library or around art. My niece noticed how much I've been struggling lately and convinced me to come in and talk to someone.

You mentioned that you can't shake this heavy, empty mood even when doing things you normally enjoy, like being at the library or around art; can you tell me more about what you mean by that, and have you lost interest in all activities that usually bring you pleasure?

It’s like a heavy, hollow feeling in my chest, as if someone turned the color down on everything, and even shelving books or looking at art just reminds me of how empty my apartment is without my wife. I've completely lost interest in other things I used to love, too, like my walking club, Zumba, and going to museums with my book-club friends. I just don't have the heart for any of it right now.
How long have you been experiencing this heavy, empty mood and loss of interest in activities since your wife and you separated?

This current heavy, empty spell has been hanging over me steadily for about three months now. It started right around the time our separation became official and I moved into my new apartment alone. It's just been a constant weight since then.
Have you experienced any periods of improvement or significant relief from this heavy, empty mood during these three months, or has it been consistently present?

No, it has been consistently present without any real relief. Every single day has felt just as heavy and gray, whether I'm trying to work at the library or look at art. There haven't been any breaks or better days since I moved into the apartment.
Have you experienced any days during these three months where you felt even slightly better or had moments of pleasure, or has it been a completely unrelenting experience?

It has been completely unrelenting, without a single day where I felt better or found any pleasure. Even trying to look at art, which used to bring me joy, now just reminds me of how empty my life is without my wife.

You've mentioned this has been going on for three months without any relief, but can you tell me if you've had any similar episodes of feeling this heavy, empty mood before in your life, or is this the first time you've experienced something like this?

Looking back, I’ve actually experienced these dragging lows, alternating with highly revved-up stretches, coming and going for many years. However, they have become much more intense and noticeable over the past year as my marriage was falling apart. This current three-month empty spell is just the most steady and heavy it has ever been.
Can you describe the 'highly revved-up stretches' you mentioned, and how they compare to your current low mood in terms of intensity, duration, and impact on your daily life?

Those revved-up stretches only last a few days, making me feel wired, sleep only three or four hours without feeling tired, and impulsively start multiple projects with high confidence. In contrast, this current low mood has dragged on steadily for three months, leaving me feeling heavy, slow, and completely drained. While the high periods make me erratic but hyperactive, these low stretches have caused me to fall behind at work and completely pull away from my friends.
Can you tell me more about how often these 'highly revved-up stretches' occur and whether they seem to be triggered by anything in particular, such as stress or significant life events?

These high-energy stretches have actually been happening off and on for many years, but they became much more frequent and intense over the past year. The gradual breakdown of my marriage and our final separation were definitely the major triggers that seemed to make these ups and downs much more tightly wound and noticeable. It felt like the stress of the breakup just magnified the whole cycle.
Do you find that your highly revved-up stretches and low mood episodes tend to cycle back and forth, or do they occur more randomly without a clear pattern?

Yes, they definitely cycle back and forth and have been doing so for many years rather than being completely random. Over the last year, as my marriage fell apart, I've noticed that these oscillations have tightened up and become much more intense and noticeable.
During these highly revved-up stretches, have you ever experienced any symptoms like excessive spending, reckless behavior, or impulsive decisions that you later regretted?

No, I haven't really experienced things like excessive spending or reckless behavior during those high-energy periods. I might get overly excited about starting new art projects or organizing things, but I haven't made any impulsive decisions that I ended up regretting later.
Have you noticed any changes in your irritability levels during either the low mood episodes or the highly revved-up stretches?

Yes, during those high-energy stretches, I can get oddly upbeat but also very snappish and irritable over minor things. I might be cracking jokes and talking a mile a minute, and then suddenly snap at a coworker for something small like mis-shelving a book. It is really unlike my usual self, but that irritability definitely flares up when I'm in those revved-up states.

Can you describe how your energy levels and motivation change when you shift from a low mood episode to a highly revved-up stretch, and do you notice any distinct triggers or patterns that precede these shifts?

During my low periods, my body feels like it's moving through molasses and I struggle to even shelf books, whereas in my revved-up phases, I'm filled with restless energy, starting multiple projects at once and staying active late into the night. As for triggers, while these cycles have occurred for years, they became much more intense and noticeable over the past year, directly coinciding with the deterioration and final separation of my marriage.
Can you estimate how many days in a row you typically experience these highly revved-up stretches before you start to feel a shift back towards a low mood episode?

Typically, those highly revved-up stretches last for just a few days, usually around three or four days at a time. After that short burst of intense energy, the high feeling starts to fade, and I eventually shift back down into my lower mood.

Can you clarify if these cycles of high and low mood episodes have ever occurred without any identifiable stressor or significant life event, or have they always seemed to be triggered by something specific, like your recent marital separation?

Yes, these cycles have been coming and going for many years, long before the separation, and in the past I didn't have any major triggers and just chalked them up to my personality or normal work stress. However, while they used to happen without any big life events, the stress of my marriage falling apart this past year has made them much more intense, frequent, and harder to ignore.

You've described both high and low mood episodes, but can you clarify if you've ever had a period of at least two weeks where you felt consistently in a normal mood, without either the high or low symptoms, especially considering the cycling pattern of your mood episodes?

I'm not really sure if I've ever had a clear two-week period where I felt completely balanced and "normal." Because I always just chalked these shifts up to my personality and work stress, I never paid close enough attention to know if there was ever a distinct, steady middle ground in between the highs and lows.

Can you try to estimate the longest period you've ever had where you didn't experience either a high or a low mood episode, to help clarify if you've ever had an extended period of what might be considered a 'normal' or euthymic mood?

I'm really not quite sure. Looking back, it feels like these ups and downs have been cycling for so many years that it's hard to pinpoint a long stretch where I felt completely stable or "normal" without one or the other. They have just been a constant background in my life for as long as I can remember.

Can you estimate the average time between the end of one low mood episode and the start of the next, or between the end of a high-energy stretch and the start of another, to help understand the pattern and frequency of these cycles?

I'm not really sure about the exact average time, as I've never tracked the cycles closely enough to give a precise number of weeks or months between them. They've been coming and going for many years, but they have definitely become much more frequent and intense since my marriage started falling apart.

Can you confirm whether you have experienced at least one major depressive episode that lasted for at least two weeks without any intervening periods of hypomania or mania, to help distinguish between the different types of mood disorders we're considering?

Yes, I can confirm that. This current low, heavy mood has been going on steadily and continuously for about three months now, ever since the separation. During this entire stretch, I haven't had any of those high-energy or wired phases breaking it up—it has just been a constant, heavy cloud.
Can you confirm if you have experienced any periods of at least two months of hypomanic symptoms without any depressive episodes, to help clarify the nature of your mood cycles?

No, I've never had those high-energy periods last for months; they typically only last for a few days at a time. It's actually my low, heavy spells that drag on for much longer, like this current one which has lasted for three months.
Have you ever had a period where you experienced both depressive and hypomanic symptoms simultaneously, or do your high and low episodes always occur separately?

No, they have always occurred separately as distinct phases rather than at the same time. I will have stretches of feeling wired, upbeat, and full of restless energy for a few days, and then at other times I experience this heavy, dragging empty mood, but the two never overlap.

Can you confirm if any of your high-energy stretches have significantly impacted your daily life or relationships in a negative way, such as causing problems at work or straining relationships with friends or family?

My high-energy periods haven't caused major, severe disruptions at work or ruined my relationships, though they do cause some mild strain. During those times, I can get irritable and snap at coworkers over small things, and my niece teases me because I talk so fast without letting others get a word in. The really significant negative impacts, like calling out sick and letting my library work pile up, have mostly happened during my recent low, heavy periods.
Have you ever experienced a period where you had symptoms of both depression and hypomania at the same time, such as feeling sad or empty but also restless or irritable?

No, I haven't really experienced those feelings at the exact same time. For me, the restless, high-energy periods and the heavy, empty moods have always happened in completely separate, distinct stretches.
Can you confirm if your current three-month low mood episode is the longest you've ever experienced, or have you had longer periods of depression in the past?
I'm not quite sure if I've had longer stretches of low mood in the past. However, this current three-month period definitely feels like the most intense and difficult one I can remember.

Have you ever had a period where your high-energy stretches were so intense that they caused significant problems in your daily life, relationships, or work, despite not necessarily being as long-lasting as your low mood episodes?

During those high-energy stretches, I actually felt quite productive and didn't see them as a problem myself, though they did cause some friction like snapping at library coworkers or talking so fast my niece could barely get a word in. While those phases caused some tension, the most severe problems with missing work and isolating myself have definitely been during my current low mood. My niece did confront me recently, though, because the overall ups and downs have become much more intense since the separation.
Can you try to recall if there was ever a year in your life where you didn't experience any significant high or low mood episodes, to help understand the overall pattern of your mood cycles?

Honestly, it's hard to recall a full year completely free of these ups and downs because they have been coming and going for so many years. In the past, I didn't pay much attention to them because I just chalked them up to personality quirks or work stress, but looking back, it's been a long-standing pattern that only became truly intense and disruptive over this past year.

Can you confirm if you have experienced at least one major depressive episode that lasted for at least two weeks without any intervening periods of hypomania or mania, and also if you have had periods of hypomania that lasted for at least four consecutive days?

Yes, I can confirm that. This current heavy, empty mood has been going on steadily for about three months now, which is much longer than two weeks, without any high periods at all. As for the high periods, those stretches of feeling wired and upbeat usually last for about three or four days at a time where the high energy is constant.
Can you estimate how many times you've experienced these distinct high-energy stretches in the past year, and how they compare in frequency and intensity to the periods of low mood?

I've experienced those high-energy stretches off and on multiple times over the past year, especially as my marriage deteriorated, and they usually feel like short, intense bursts of being buzzed and wired for a few days at a time. In contrast, my low moods are much longer and heavier, like this current empty spell that has been dragging on steadily for about three months now.
Have you ever experienced any symptoms of increased self-esteem or grandiosity during your high-energy stretches?

Yes, during those high-energy periods, I do get a real boost in my confidence. I catch myself thinking that I'm wasted as just a library assistant and could easily run the whole branch or build a massive online arts community. Looking back, though, I realize those thoughts sound a bit over the top for a guy my age.

Can you clarify if the duration and intensity of your high-energy stretches have changed over time, especially in relation to the frequency and duration of your low mood episodes, and if there's any noticeable pattern to how these episodes cycle?

Yes, I've had these cycles of highs and lows for many years, but they have become much more frequent and intense—almost like the oscillations have tightened—over the past year since my marriage fell apart. Currently, this heavy low mood has been dragging on steadily for about three months, whereas those high-energy phases typically only last for a few days at a time.

Can you describe any differences in how your high-energy stretches and low mood episodes have affected your relationships, work, or daily activities over time, especially considering the recent changes since your separation?

During my high-energy phases, I would stay up late blogging, reorganize everything, and feel confident enough to run the whole library branch. In contrast, during this low spell since the separation, I feel like I'm moving through molasses, letting my work backlog pile up, calling out sick, and I've completely withdrawn from my walking and book clubs. These ups and downs have happened for years, but they have become much more intense and damaging to my life since my marriage ended.
